goal: Make the worker's Claude session id a parent-side fact: emit exactly one new flag pair, --session-id <record.dispatch_id>, from scripts/cmux/record.mjs's buildArgv, and move every argv-shape test pin that this changes. No new record field, no schema change, no schema_version bump — dispatch_id is ALREADY a parent-minted, pattern-validated, never-reused v4 UUID, which is precisely why it can be reused as the session id. This is a three-line edit to the repo's security-audited argv surface, and it must be reviewed as an argv change, not waved through as wiring.
constraints: buildArgv (scripts/cmux/record.mjs:639-679) is 'the ONLY argv source' (asserted at scripts/cmux/adapter-claude.mjs:45-48) and carries the PRE-1C-VERIFY hard-rule set in its own header. All nine hard rules stay intact; the three that this edit is near must be re-asserted, not merely left alone: rule 1 (a bare '--' immediately before the prompt positional), rule 2 (the role prompt passed as a PATH, never as bytes), rule 3 (each permission rule is its own argv element).

PLACEMENT IS LOAD-BEARING: push --session-id immediately after the --model / --effort pair and BEFORE --permission-mode and every variadic flag (--tools, --allowedTools, --disallowedTools, --add-dir), i.e. far before the bare '--'. conventions.md 2026-08-01: those flags are variadic and greedily consume the following positional; a flag placed after them can be swallowed, and the failure is SILENT (SessionStart fires, UserPromptSubmit never does, indefinite idle).

The value is record.dispatch_id read straight off the validated record — never a second mint, never randomUUID() at this site, never a value derived from anything the worker can influence. readRecord's schema validation already guarantees a well-formed UUID before argv build (scripts/cmux/dispatch-record.schema.json:10 pins the strict UUID pattern).
The existing newline/CR sweep (record.mjs:672-676) must keep covering the new element — do not move, narrow, or short-circuit it. Its refusal is a runtime throw, not just a test assertion.

NO SCHEMA CHANGE. dispatch-record.schema.json is untouched, schema_version stays 2, and `flags` stays the closed two-boolean object it is (dispatch-record.schema.json:22-30, required both keys, additionalProperties:false) — it is not a pass-through channel and must not be made one.

Nonce hygiene is untouched: assertNoNonce (applied at record.mjs:606) and every assertNoNonce-class assertion must still be green against the new argv. conventions.md 2026-08-02: 'never logs the secret' is vacuous unless proven by mutation — assert against NONCE_PREFIX on the new argv path too, not only the happy path.

conventions.md 2026-08-01: no typecheck/lint tooling exists in this repo — validation is the filtered test run only.

discovery_context:
WHAT THIS IS. Issue #41 (SF-2, epic #39) mirrors a cmux run into the ledger; the mirror needs to know the worker's Claude session id in order to (a) find its transcript and (b) heartbeat its agent_sessions row. The design of record is .claude/dev-team/tasks/issue-41/architecture-package-v1.md (Fork B / ADR-026 clause 3). This spec is self-contained without it.

THE ONE EDIT. Pattern to mirror is the function itself — scripts/cmux/record.mjs:639-666:
  export function buildArgv(record) {
    const argv = []
    argv.push('--model', record.model)
    if (record.effort !== null) {
      argv.push('--effort', record.effort)
    }
    argv.push('--permission-mode', record.profile.permission_mode)
    // Hard rule 2: the role prompt is passed as a PATH, never as bytes.
    argv.push('--append-system-prompt-file', record.role_prompt_path)
    argv.push('--tools', TOOLS_JOIN === 'comma' ? record.tools.join(',') : record.tools.join(' '))
    // Hard rule 3: each permission rule is its own argv element.
    argv.push('--allowedTools', ...record.profile.allow)
    argv.push('--disallowedTools', ...record.disallowed_tools)
    ...
    argv.push('--add-dir', ...ADD_DIRS(record))
    // Hard rule 1: a bare -- immediately before the prompt positional.
    argv.push('--', record.kickoff)
Insert exactly one line after the --effort block (i.e. before --permission-mode):
    argv.push('--session-id', record.dispatch_id)
The sweep that follows is what makes the new element safe for free — record.mjs:672-676:
  for (const el of argv) {
    if (/[\n\r]/.test(el)) {
      throw new Error(`buildArgv: refused — argv element contains a newline or carriage return: ${JSON.stringify(el)}`)
    }
  }

WHY dispatch_id AND NOT A NEW FIELD. newDispatchId() is randomUUID() (record.mjs:155); dispatch-record.schema.json:10 pins it to the strict UUID pattern; the schema's own description says it is never reused, and a retry mints a fresh one. readRecord validates the parsed record against that schema and refuses (RecordInvalidError) before argv build, so the value reaching --session-id is already a well-formed UUID. The alternative — mint a second UUID and carry it in the record — was BLOCKED because `flags` is a closed two-boolean object (dispatch-record.schema.json:22-30: required both keys, additionalProperties:false, two boolean/const:true properties), so no pass-through channel exists, and adding a field would mean a schema_version bump on a frozen, security-audited contract plus a contract-freeze review panel. conventions.md's own lesson applies: reuse an existing already-validated identifier before minting a new one; a schema's closed shape is a design signal, not an obstacle to route around.

LIVE-VERIFIED, SO THIS IS NOT A DOCS GUESS (issue #41 architecture package section 12, orchestrator, 2026-08-09, installed CLI 2.1.225, three spawnSync probes in probeSystemPromptFile's shape — scripts/cmux/adapter-claude.mjs:277-291 — deliberately no --help, no --version):
  1. `claude --session-id not-a-valid-uuid-value` -> exit 1, stderr 'Error: Invalid session ID. Must be a valid UUID.' The flag is RECOGNIZED AND VALIDATED, not rejected as unknown.
  2. `claude --session-id <fresh v4 uuid>` (no -p) -> exit 1 with a stdin/print-mode message unrelated to --session-id, confirming the flag parsed cleanly past that point.
  3. `claude --session-id <fresh uuid> -p 'reply with exactly the word: ok'` -> exit 0, stdout 'ok', and the transcript landed at exactly ~/.claude/projects/-Users-x-Development-dev-team-claude-plugin/<that-uuid>.jsonl, found by a plain filename scan (no dash-encoding derivation).
So B4 ships unconditionally; there is no fallback branch to write. A reused id was not exercised and is not reachable today (retries mint a fresh dispatch_id) — that is a stated assumption, not a case to design for.

WHY PREFLIGHT DOES NOT GATE THIS (checked live, so don't add a gate): preflight() (scripts/cmux/cmuxctl.mjs:415+) checks the cmux binary's own RPC capabilities and, separately, that each roster role's adapter CLI is merely PRESENT on PATH (adapter_present, a boolean). isValidPreflightCache's frozen shape (cmuxctl.mjs:389-403) has no `supports` field, and adapter-claude.mjs's own `capabilities` verb (the one carrying a supports map) is never invoked from preflight(), dispatchCmd, or anywhere in cmuxctl.mjs — only from test/claude-adapter.test.mjs. So --session-id support CANNOT be preflight-gated today without new work, and adding that is out of scope. Do not add a preflight check, a capability probe, or a runtime feature test.

GOTCHAS THAT WOULD OTHERWISE COST YOU A GREP: (1) the kickoff literally begins 'Dispatch <dispatch_id>.' (record.mjs:390) — that is a legacy discovery token, unrelated to this change; leave it alone. (2) buildArgv's header names two UNVERIFIED composition constants (TOOLS_JOIN at record.mjs:620, ADD_DIRS at :625) — do not touch them. (3) adapter-claude.mjs never composes argv (:45-48) and is NOT in scope: if you find yourself editing it, stop and return `insufficient`. (4) conventions.md 2026-08-08: verify the citations above resolve on THIS branch before relying on them — this branch is cut from main, where all of record.mjs, dispatch-record.schema.json and the fixture exist.

interface_contract:
CONSUMED HERE (produced by be-41-02) — referenced, never redefined:

=== C3 — TranscriptResolution ===
resolveTranscript({record, projectsDir}) -> {claude_session_id, transcript_path} | null
Under ADR-026 clause 3 this is findTranscript(projectsDir, record.dispatch_id)'s scan (scripts/task-cost-log.mjs:109-129) with its refusal posture converted from throw to null: 0 matches -> null plus stats.resolution_missing++ (EXPECTED on early ticks, so NOT logged per tick); >1 matches -> null plus stats.resolution_ambiguous++ plus one log line, NEVER a guess. Never derive the project-dir dash-encoding (that module's header rule). Called once per unresolved dispatch per await tick; the result is PINNED on first success and never re-resolved, so a transcript later forked, rotated or duplicated cannot move the answer.

WHAT THIS SLICE CONTRIBUTES TO THAT CONTRACT: claude_session_id === record.dispatch_id, by construction, because buildArgv passes --session-id <record.dispatch_id> to the worker. This is the ONE fact the resolver's scan key depends on, and this slice is its only producer. Consequences other slices rely on: (adw_id, claude_session_id) is unique per dispatch by construction, so ledger.mjs's UNIQUE(adw_id, claude_session_id) + INSERT OR IGNORE can never silently collapse two dispatches, and a retry (fresh dispatch_id) gets its own row; and because the id is known BEFORE the pane exists, ledger.heartbeat's UPDATE ... WHERE adw_id = ? AND claude_session_id = ? (scripts/factory/ledger.mjs:956) is satisfiable from the first await tick (be-41-04).

NO NEW SHAPE IS PRODUCED BY THIS SLICE: no record field, no schema key, no export. The dispatch record's on-disk shape is byte-identical before and after.
